params.body:
Guilherme sent new versions of all 78 posts as PDFs on 15 October. The live posts should take the new text and pictures without losing their address, date, cover, tags or citations, the 16 that never went live should go live with them, the dates should be spread again so the site's newest post is current, and every post's trend citations should be checked against its new text. This PR adds the tools for that run; the run itself happens on the box with a data bundle, after merge.

## What changes

**`bin/import-articles.mjs --replace`** (with `--match`, `--run`, `--undo-replace`)
- The importer refuses to overwrite a non-draft on purpose; `--replace` is the one explicit exception, and it prints what it replaces and what it keeps.
- Replaced from the file: title, body, opportunity, reading time. A standfirst is only filled when it is empty or cut off: the converter derives it, and one an editor wrote stays.
- Kept: id (so the address on gentells.com), status, published_at, featured_at, cover, tier, byline, tags, elements, notes, views and citations. Each citation's anchor follows its sentence into the new text, or is cleared when the sentence is gone.
- Old text and anchors go into `article_replace_undo`, each post gets a version step, and `--undo-replace=<run>` puts a run back.
- A body that still holds an unplaced `IMAGE:` reference is refused.

**`bin/posts-to-json.mjs`**
- Image names are made safe. A PDF called `Name (1).pdf` gave names whose `)` ended the markdown reference: eight posts were refused, and names with spaces left placeholders in the body.
- Pictures are written as JPEG q85 (no chroma subsampling) at most 1600 px wide, PNG only where there is transparency. Lossless PNG at PDF resolution came to 134 MB over the 78 posts, up to 4 MB a picture; now 20 MB.

**`bin/redate-posts.mjs`** (new)
- Spreads the published posts evenly from `--from` to `--to`, one a day at 09:00 Brussels, order kept. updated_at moves so the site takes the change.
- `--publish=<file>` puts named pieces live in the same run, after the dated ones. A piece without a cover gets the first picture of its pool, as all 39 chosen covers are; an entry may correct guessed topics.
- `article_redate_undo` keeps dates, status, cover and tags; `--undo=<run>`.

**`bin/relink-evidence.mjs`** (new)
- Applies a reviewed plan of removed and added trend citations. Refused before anything is written when a trend is not public (linking it would publish it), when the sentence is not in the post, when a note lacks "linked <date>: ", or when a removal has no reason.
- Names every trend that stops being public, keeps `article_evidence_relink_undo`, `--undo=<run>`.

## Checks

- New and changed tests: `import-articles`, `post-pdf`, `redate-posts`, `relink-evidence` (23, all passing).
- Full suite 1209/1215; the 6 are `report-render`, which needs `pdftoppm` and fails the same way on main.
- Rehearsed on a read-only export of production (80 posts, 94 citations): 78 replaced, 78 dated with 16 published, 51 citations removed and 6 added, all 78 pass gentells.com's tagging gate, and the Studio's writing view reads every picture and heading as a block. Running the three undos in reverse gives back the export exactly.

Nothing runs at deploy. The run waits for the bundle and is done by hand on the box, each step with `--dry` first.
params.title: Replace posts in place from the author's PDFs, re-date them, relink their evidence
